_doc: Revert-verify mutants for #4473 — `GroundingExecutor`'s BODY write channels (`replaceBody` / `extractBody`, reached by the `body_template` grounding step and by `create_instance`'s `cloneTargetBody` + `userInput.body` literal path). Run from the repo root after replacing the path placeholders: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file>. Axis names are A<N>, matching the test titles.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/services/GroundingExecutor.ts
_note_control_axes: A4 (LF byte-parity) and A7/A8/A9 carry NO mutant of their own BY DESIGN, and that is their product rather than a hole (integration-test-revert-verify §A118). A4's subject is that the conversion changed NOTHING on the LF path, so a mutant restoring the pre-#4473 implementation must leave it GREEN — its silence under M1/M2/M3 IS the parity proof. A7/A8 are the same statement for `extractBody` (CRLF/LF were already correct before the fix). A9 pins the pre-existing `req 454ccedf` axis B8 contract (a frontmatter-less target invents no block), which this work item did not change either.

M1_replaceBody_restores_the_local_narrow._note: The IDENTITY-LOSS half of #4473, isolated: the seam logic is kept intact so only the PREDICATE narrows. `\r?\n` needs at least one `\n` and `^---` cannot reach past a BOM, so a lone-CR / BOM asset falls into `return body` and the file loses its frontmatter. A3 (the CRLF seam) must stay GREEN here — that is what makes this mutant's red set distinguishable from M2's. ⛤ This mutant is also what proved A10 was VACUOUS for the identity defect on its first run: the round trip CLOSED on the corrupted asset, because a frontmatter-less intermediate makes `extractBody` return the whole file, so `extractBody(replaceBody(x)) === x` held while the asset's identity was gone. A10 now asserts the trip happens on an ASSET, which is why it is in this expect-set at all.

M2_replaceBody_restores_the_bare_LF_seam._note: The SEAM half, isolated: the predicate stays shared (so A1/A2 keep their frontmatter) and only the inserted line ending reverts to an unconditional LF — the mixed-terminator defect on every CRLF asset. Type-preserving: still a template literal of three string parts.

M3_extractBody_restores_the_local_narrow._note: The mirror defect: with no match the WHOLE source file is returned as `the body`, so `cloneTargetBody` copies the source's frontmatter INTO the clone's body. This is why A5/A6 assert on the BODY half specifically — a whole-file `toContain("exo__Asset_uid")` is satisfied by the corruption itself.

M4_extractBody_slices_by_the_reconstruct._note: `end` is the offset in the ORIGINAL string; `text.length` is the length of a block whose BOM RUN was normalised to one. They differ by exactly the collapsed bytes, so a 2-BOM source leaks a dash of the closing fence into the body — the defect `get-body` shipped before #4469. Reddens A6 ALONE: with a 0- or 1-BOM source the two values coincide, which is why A10's BOM leg (one BOM) stays green and the axis is adressed rather than ambient.

M5_leading_eol_cannot_strip_a_lone_CR._note: The third, quietest half: even with the right predicate and the right offset, `/^\r?\n/` cannot swallow a lone-CR seam (it is indivisible and needs an `\n`), so the separator stays glued to the first body line. Only a BYTE-EXACT body assertion sees this — a `toContain` would not, which is why A5/A6 were tightened to `toBe`.
